Last week, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that its former employee "for the benefit of OpenAI" stole trade secrets.

It is reported that in the process, Apple has directly sent letters to dozens of former employees currently working at OpenAI.

According to the Financial Times, Apple has issued evidence preservation notices to approximately 40 former employees.

An evidence preservation notice is a formal written notification sent to individuals or organizations, requiring them to preserve documents, records, and other evidence that may be related to legal disputes. Such letters typically specify what should be preserved.

This move stems from Apple's suspicion that the theft of trade secrets may involve more than just the defendants listed in last week's initial lawsuit.

As a reminder, Apple's lawsuit lists OpenAI and io Products as defendants, along with former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan.
